nodes.name: 3D Modeling
nodes.description: Sculpting and constructing digital surfaces — polygon meshes, NURBS, and subdivision surfaces — that form characters, props, and environments. The geometric foundation of the 3D pipeline.

nodes.name: Texturing & Shading
nodes.description: Painting surface detail — color, roughness, bump, displacement — and defining material responses to light via UV mapping and procedural shaders.

nodes.name: Rigging
nodes.description: Building the digital skeleton and control systems (joints, IK/FK, blendshapes) that let animators pose characters and creatures.

nodes.name: 3D Lighting
nodes.description: Placing and tuning virtual lights — key, fill, rim, HDRI image-based lighting — to define mood, depth, and realism in a scene.

nodes.name: Rendering
nodes.description: Converting 3D scenes to final images: offline ray tracing and path tracing for film, real-time rasterization for games and virtual production.

nodes.name: Dynamics & Simulation
nodes.description: Physically based animation of cloth, hair, fluids, particles, and destruction using solvers rather than manual keyframing.

nodes.name: Motion Tracking
nodes.description: Recovering the 3D camera movement from live-action footage so CG elements can be inserted with matching perspective.

nodes.name: Match Moving
nodes.description: Aligning virtual cameras and geometry to real footage frame-by-frame for seamless CG/live-action integration.

nodes.name: CG Integration
nodes.description: Merging rendered CG elements into live-action plates with consistent lighting, shadows, and lens characteristics.

nodes.name: Particle Effects
nodes.description: Simulating dust, smoke, sparks, water, and debris with particle systems for explosions and environmental effects.

nodes.name: Crowd Simulation
nodes.description: Generating large-scale crowds and armies procedurally via agent-based simulation, used for battles and stadium scenes.

nodes.name: Set Extension
nodes.description: Digitally extending practical sets and matte paintings into vast environments — cities, landscapes, historical reconstructions.

nodes.name: Animation Director
nodes.description: Leads the creative vision of an animated production, guiding story, performance, and visual style across the pipeline.

nodes.name: Storyboard Artist
nodes.description: Draws the pre-visualization of shots — camera, staging, timing — that becomes the blueprint for animation.

nodes.name: Layout Artist
nodes.description: Establishes shot composition, camera moves, and staging before animation begins.

nodes.name: Key Animator
nodes.description: Draws or poses the defining keyframes of a character's movement, defining timing and performance.

nodes.name: Inbetween Artist
nodes.description: Draws the intermediate frames between keyframes to create smooth motion — the bulk of traditional 2D animation labor.

nodes.name: Background Artist
nodes.description: Paints the environments and backdrops behind animated characters, establishing world and atmosphere.

nodes.name: Animation Producer
nodes.description: Manages budget, schedule, and crew of an animation production, coordinating studios and delivery.

nodes.description: Three-dimensional representations conveying how a design will appear to the eye.

nodes.name: Physical Modeling
nodes.description: Scaled three-dimensional models in wood, cardboard, or 3D printing for design study and presentation.

nodes.name: Yangban
nodes.description: The hereditary aristocratic class of Joseon Korea that monopolized official posts and land through the Confucian civil-service examinations. Collapsed with the abolition of the class system under Japanese rule.

nodes.name: Hwarang
nodes.description: An elite youth warrior order of the Silla kingdom, blending martial training with Buddhist and Confucian moral cultivation. Central to Silla's unification of the Korean peninsula.

nodes.name: Devaraja (God-King)
nodes.description: The divine-kingship office of the Khmer Empire, in which the ruler was identified with a deity and legitimized by monumental temple-mountains such as Angkor Wat. Coordinated the irrigation systems that sustained the empire.

nodes.name: Mongol Khan
nodes.description: The elected supreme ruler of the Mongol Empire, chosen at a kurultai and bound by the yassa legal code. Commanded the largest contiguous land empire in history via a decimal army and the yam courier relay.

nodes.name: Sogdian Merchant
nodes.description: Iranian-speaking merchants of Sogdiana who dominated Silk Road trade between China and the West. Their caravan networks also transmitted Buddhism, Manichaeism, and writing systems across Central Asia.

nodes.name: Mesopotamian Scribe
nodes.description: The cuneiform scribes who produced the earliest written records of humanity — contracts, tax accounts, and literature. Trained in the edubba school, they formed a literate elite at the core of Mesopotamian temple and palace administration.

nodes.name: Aksumite King (Negus)
nodes.description: The monarch of the Aksumite Empire, a major Red Sea trading power and among the first states to adopt Christianity. Issued its own coinage and erected monumental stelae.

nodes.name: Griot / Jali
nodes.description: Hereditary oral historians, musicians, and praise-singers of the Mande peoples of West Africa. As living archives, they preserved royal genealogies and epics such as Sundiata for centuries before writing.

nodes.name: Quipucamayoc
nodes.description: Specialists of the Inca Empire who encoded census, tribute, and historical data on quipu — knotted cords using a positional decimal system. A bureaucratic memory apparatus that functioned entirely without writing.

functions: recorded census and tribute on quipu

nodes.name: Chasqui Runner
nodes.description: Highly trained relay runners of the Inca Empire who carried messages and goods along the 40,000-km Qhapaq Ñan road network. Teams at tambo posts relayed information across the Andes in days.

nodes.name: Maya Scribe
nodes.description: Literate elite specialists of the Classic Maya who composed hieroglyphic texts recording dynastic histories, astronomy, and ritual on stone monuments and bark-paper codices. Their script is the most complete writing system of the pre-Columbian Americas.

nodes.name: Vestal Virgin
nodes.description: Priestesses of Vesta who tended Rome's sacred hearth, on whose purity the city's fate was believed to depend. Held unusual legal autonomy in a deeply patriarchal society.

nodes.name: Janissary
nodes.description: The elite standing infantry of the Ottoman Empire, originally recruited through the devshirme levy of Christian boys. Among Europe's first professional gunpowder armies; disbanded by force in 1826.

nodes.name: Mamluk
nodes.description: Enslaved soldiers, mostly Turkic and Circassian, who rose to become the ruling military elite of Egypt. Defeated the Mongols at Ain Jalut in 1260 and ruled a sultanate until the 16th century.

nodes.name: Viking Raider
nodes.description: Seaborne Norse warriors who raided, traded, and settled from Ireland to the Caspian and reached North America. The longship's shallow draft made their mobility decisive.

nodes.name: Scholar-Official (Shidafu)
nodes.description: The Confucian scholar-bureaucrats selected by the imperial examinations who administered China for over a millennium. Fused political office with moral and literary authority.

nodes.name: Mechanical Calculator Operator
nodes.description: Operated mechanical calculators and tabulating machines (Comptometer, Hollerith) before electronic computers.

nodes.name: Computer Operator
nodes.description: Operated early mainframe/electronic computers via punched cards and consoles, 1950s-1980s.

nodes.name: AI Model Development
nodes.description: Training and fine-tuning foundation models and LLMs — the compute- and capital-intensive core of modern AI. Dominated by a few frontier labs; billion-dollar-scale training runs.

nodes.name: AI Infrastructure
nodes.description: The GPU/TPU clusters, interconnects, and data pipelines that make model training possible. Includes cloud AI compute, HPC fabrics, and vector databases; the 'picks and shovels' layer.

nodes.name: Applied AI Solutions
nodes.description: Vertical AI products: medical imaging AI, fraud detection, autonomous driving, customer-service agents, code assistants. Where AI meets specific industries and revenue.

nodes.name: Edge & On-Device AI
nodes.description: Inference on phones, cameras, vehicles, and industrial sensors rather than cloud. Driven by NPU chips, privacy, and latency; fast-growing.

nodes.name: AI Safety & Alignment
nodes.description: Evaluating and aligning frontier models: red-teaming, interpretability, governance, and safety tooling. A small but strategically critical segment.

nodes.name: Generative AI & Synthetic Media
nodes.description: Text, image, video, audio, and code generation products. Consumer and enterprise; the most visible AI market (ChatGPT-class tools).

nodes.name: Private Equity
nodes.description: Buyout and growth investing in private companies: leveraged buyouts, restructuring, and operational value creation. Large pools of committed capital.

nodes.name: Venture Capital
nodes.description: Early-stage equity investment in startups, concentrated in tech and life sciences. High risk, outsized-return model; fuels innovation ecosystems.
